consensus_summary: Primary meaning is the four cardinal directions as a merism for the totality/universal scope of the earth (gathering, scattering, or forces operating worldwide); heavenly agents/spirits (Zech 6), judgment forces, and life-giving breath are secondary contextual alternatives.
book_summary: The four winds are the four spirits of heaven—God's executing agents—shown as the four horsemen, with the same fourfold outgoing pattern in the river dividing from Eden.
consensus_core_identification: four cardinal directions signifying earthly totality/universal scope
book_core_identification: God's executing agents (four spirits of heaven) manifested as the four horsemen
boundary_disagreement: Consensus keeps the agents/spirits reading secondary and never equates it to the Rev 6 horsemen or Eden river heads; book makes that specific agent-horsemen identity definitional and drops the directional core.
material_contradiction: Directional-universality idiom and personal executing agents (= horsemen) cannot both be the primary referent of 'four winds' in the same sense; adopting the book replaces the consensus core.
rationale: Consensus settles on compass-point totality as the core (with agents only an alternative from Zech 6:5). Book elevates and re-identifies the term as the spirits/agents expressly shown as the four horsemen plus Eden parallel, a replacement not a boundary adjustment of the same referent.
strongest_objection: Rev 6 horsemen and Rev 7/Zech winds remain distinct images in standard reading; printed texts supply components but no equation of winds to horsemen.
